_why_arch_scan_and_descriptor: plugins/harness-gates/lib/arch-scan.mjs 169 → 175; plugins/harness-gates/lib/descriptor.mjs 104 → 106. arch-scan and descriptor.mjs both received the run ledger. arch-scan emits a ratchet record at the moment a budget moves, in either direction, which is the whole point of inlining measurement: a retro that reconstructs its timeline afterwards pays for the reconstruction every time and can only ever see what survived. descriptor.mjs gained metricsFile because it is the single place descriptor defaults live. Do not recover these lines by moving the emit to a wrapper that has to be remembered, or by re-deriving the ledger path at the call site.
_why_arch_scan_received_accept: plugins/harness-gates/lib/arch-scan.mjs 118 → 169. arch-scan received --accept itself: the ratchet had a codified path in one direction only, so recording a justified raise meant hand-editing JSON — done four times in one session, once wrongly because the violation block goes to stderr. This is the right home because the scanner already knows which files are over and by how much; a separate tool would re-derive that and drift. Do not recover these lines by removing the reason requirement, which is the rail that makes the command safer than the hand-edit it replaces.
_why_auto: 146 → 156: --auto used to commit the adoption straight to the default branch, then print a handover telling the adopter to enable a ruleset requiring pull requests — stranding that commit where it can no longer be pushed. It now creates chore/adopt-the-harness first, and warns that harness-preflight will refuse the adoption commit BY DESIGN (adoption is the one change that legitimately writes .github/workflows/ and .claude/settings.json). Both are new behaviour; the prose in the file was cut first. Do not recover these lines by dropping the branch step.
_why_configs: 73 → 104: scriptsFor() moved here from bootstrap.mjs and became descriptor-aware. The first adoption into a JavaScript repo handed it `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` and a verify that ran it, so the adopter's very first verify failed on a file they do not have, for a language they do not use, in a script the harness had just written. This module's job is exactly 'render config from the descriptor', so it is the right home; bootstrap.mjs shed the table in the same change. Do not inline it back.
_why_contributor_zoning: preflight.mjs 121 → 144 and descriptor.mjs 99 → 104, both from admitting HUMAN principals to a repository whose rails were all built for processes. preflight gained a fifth refusal — zoning, the radius a named principal may write in — which is genuinely new behaviour and not sludge: territory answers 'is anyone else working here right now' and zoning answers 'is this person allowed to work here at all', and an athlete needs the first because its contract fixes its behaviour while a human needs the second because nothing fixes theirs. The model itself did NOT land here; it is in principals.mjs, and preflight calls one function. The rest of the growth is the refusal message, which now names what to do next instead of only what is wrong — a new contributor meeting a red gate alone in their first week is the failure mode this whole change is defending against, and a refusal that ends without a next step is where it starts. descriptor.mjs gained docsDir and ideasFile because the zoning table reads them and this module is the single place descriptor defaults are allowed to live; putting them anywhere else is the six-copy bug that module was created to end. Do not recover these lines by inlining zoning back into preflight or by re-deriving the descriptor at the call site.
_why_disclosure_guard: principals.mjs, standing.mjs and crossing.mjs all grew for one reason: a fresh adopter's .harness/ is NOT gitignored. It reaches their .gitignore only through harness-bootstrap, and installing the plugins does not run it — so a repository can hold a roster of real people that git will commit on the next `git add -A`, while every tool here cheerfully prints it. The harness was treating a property of ITS OWN repo as a property of the adopter's. rosterState() now distinguishes ABSENT from EXPOSED and refuses to read in the second case, and the roster schema is CLOSED to exactly {id, kind, tier, identities} so a well-meant free-text note beside a person's name has nowhere to live — you cannot leak a field no code reads. Do not recover these lines by collapsing exposed back into absent, or by widening the projection.
_why_dupe_scan: dupe-scan carries a long comment explaining what its IGNORE list does and does NOT justify. An earlier version of that comment defended six copies of the descriptor preamble on a rationale that turned out to be false; the replacement says so explicitly, because a future maintainer who trims it back would re-import the same mistake. The explanation is the point.
_why_first_adoption: auto.mjs 156 → 168 and detect.mjs 80 → 106, both from the first adoption into a repository shaped differently from this one. auto.mjs gained a step that formats WHAT THE RUN WROTE and nothing else — three files the bootstrap had written failed the formatter it had just installed, so the adopter's first verify was red for something the harness did. detect.mjs gained spec-suffix resolution: the gate file must carry the suffix the repo's OWN test command collects, because a repo globbing spec/**/*.test.js was handed gates.test.mjs and never saw it — gates reporting nothing while the suite stayed green. Both are new behaviour preventing silent failure; prose was cut first.
_why_map_and_cartography: 172 → 190 (cartography.mjs) and 24 → 33 (map.mjs): harness-map wrote a file with no doctype, so every browser opened it in quirks mode — it rendered, just not as the CSS was written for. mapDocument() adds the document skeleton; map.mjs resolves the REPOSITORY's name instead of the checkout directory's, so a worktree called `repo-2` stops appearing in the title of a shared file. Both are new behaviour, not accumulated sludge, and the prose in both files was cut first. Do not recover these lines by dropping the skeleton — a fragment written to disk is a quirks-mode document.
_why_merge_and_detect: 69 → 101 (merge.mjs) and 59 → 80 (detect.mjs): both grew because they RECEIVED a cohesive extraction out of bootstrap.mjs, which fell 238 → 209 in the same change. Total lines across the three files went DOWN. The size ratchet cannot tell 'absorbed a well-placed extraction' from 'someone piled on', so this is the justified-growth branch the scanner's own message describes. Do not trim these back by moving the code out again — mergeClaudeSettings belongs with the other two merges (it folds into a file the project owns and that carries hooks), and gateSpecFor belongs with the other repo-state detection.
_why_privacy_rail: preflight.mjs 144 → 167, standing.mjs 106 → 116, campaigns.mjs 115 → 123. A hostile review of this change found a LIVE hole the four existing refusals could not have caught: .harness/ holds the roster, the roster names real people and their email addresses, and the only thing keeping it out of a public repository was a .gitignore line. A .gitignore is not a gate — it does not stop `git add -f`, an agent, or GitHub's web editor, which commits through the API and never reads it while being the one interface /onboard tells a new contributor to use. The refusal has to ask git directly (`ls-files -- .harness/`) because changedFiles() strips .harness/ out before anything sees it, correctly, so the dangerous file was being removed from the evidence on its way in. standing.mjs grew because `reverted` now appears only in a single-principal view: in a table it is a comparison between people and there is nothing to act on in learning someone else has fewer. campaigns.mjs received the crossing. Do not recover these lines by trusting .gitignore, by re-adding .harness/ to the diff, or by putting `reverted` back in the roster-wide table.
